short: Mandarin lip-to-speech whose gain over Intelligible matches its English-initialization ablation; the tone components move CER little in single runs and pitch removal leaves TER at 40.9%.
position: The paper's three changes (English-pretrained AV-HuBERT encoder, ASR-fine-tuned unit targets, flow-matching F0 and postnet) are standard against the field. Its lowest CER and TER on CN-CVS unseen speakers hold against its five baselines, but the ablations tie the gain to the cross-lingual initialization; the tone-specific parts are not shown to matter beyond single runs, and removing the pitch predictor leaves TER unchanged. The closest prior design, V2SFlow, is not compared, the only other CN-CVS video-to-speech study is not cited, and the FunASR re-transcribed test labels come without a real-audio error floor (M11, behind).
